description: This course covers foundational and advanced concepts in Machine Learning, including supervised and unsupervised learning methods; algorithms such as linear regression, decision trees, k-means clustering, and support vector machines; deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch; and evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. It also includes topics like feature engineering, model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and ethical considerations in AI. Students will explore standard datasets from UCI and Kaggle, and apply these techniques to real-world problems using Jupyter Notebooks and cloud platforms like AWS and Google Cloud.

clos.text: Define supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms, including their mathematical foundations and applications in real-world scenarios.
Describe the architecture and operation of deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch, including their role in building neural networks.
Explain the principles of model evaluation and selection, including the use of cross-validation, confusion matrices, and ROC curves.
Apply machine learning algorithms to solve practical problems using Python libraries such as scikit-learn and pandas.
Design and implement a complete machine learning pipeline, including data preprocessing, model training, and deployment on cloud platforms.

labs: Build a logistic regression model for binary classification
Train a random forest classifier on the Iris dataset
Perform k-means clustering on the MNIST dataset

topics: Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Kernel Methods
labs: Implement SVM for text classification using TfidfVectorizer
Apply PCA for dimensionality reduction on the Wine dataset
Build a simple neural network using TensorFlow

topics: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for Image Recognition
labs: Train a CNN for image classification on the CIFAR-10 dataset
Implement an LSTM network for time series prediction
Build a VAE for image generation using TensorFlow
Deploy a machine learning model using AWS SageMaker
Tune hyperparameters using Optuna and scikit-learn
